welcome: Egypt. And a map I paid too much for.
welcome2: Somewhere on it is a pyramid nobody has finished emptying.
welcome3: The map, then. Pick a journey.
pyramidIntro: Look at these walls — so many numbers are missing!
pyramidIntro2: The secret: every number is the sum of the two below it.
pyramidIntro3: Use that, and we'll uncover what the ancient builders hid here. Good luck!
pyramidBlockedBlocks: Some blocks are blocked. They do not reveal their value.
pyramidBlockedBlocks2: We can try to calculate their value based on blocks around it.
pyramidBlockedBlocks3: And then use that number from memory.
pyramidBlockedBlocks4: You made it this far, you can do it!
expeditionCompleted2: A new expedition is now available.
collectionIntro: During our expeditions we found some items!
collectionIntro2: You can inspect them in your Collection screen.
collectionIntro3: Swipe/scroll the screen to the right to see your collection.
tombIntro2: Maybe we can translate the text using the hieroglyphs we found.
tombIntro3: We could even find a treasure here.
tombTutorial: See those symbol slots in the formulas? Place hieroglyphs from your collection below to fill them in.
tombTutorial2: The hint formulas will confirm when your assignments are correct — use them to find the right combination.
tombTutorial3: Once every slot is filled, a number lock appears. Solve the main formula to find the code and open the tomb!
hieroglyphUnlock: We have a special artifact — it lets us write on one of those sealed blocks!
hieroglyphUnlock2: Tap a glowing stone, then drag the artifact onto it to unlock it. One block per pyramid.
errorHighlightTutorial: That treasure we found has a handy trick — fill in a wrong answer and one mistake will glow red!
errorHighlightTutorial2: Only one block glows at a time, so it's still a challenge. But it helps narrow things down!
earlyFeedbackTutorial: See those checkpoint blocks? They turn green or red as you fill them in — live feedback!
earlyFeedbackTutorial2: Use them as anchors while solving. If one turns red, something nearby needs fixing.
notEnoughHieroglyphs: You can always stop this expedition by returning to the travel screen.
notEnoughHieroglyphs2: We can interrupt the expedition to search elsewhere for the hieroglyphs we still need to complete.
tombLoot: Wow, our first treasure! Well done!
mapPiece: We found a map piece! Together they lead to a hidden tomb.
mapPiece2: There's one waiting in each expedition at this difficulty — let's find them all!
mapPiece3: Check the journey list to see how many we've collected so far.
mosaicStarter: A cat in the doorway, and a snake leaving in a hurry. That was worth a bowl of milk.
mosaicStarter2: Egyptians loved cats for exactly this — they killed the snakes and the rats that got into the grain.
mosaicStarter3: They loved them so much they made one a goddess. Bastet. Protector of the house, the door, everyone asleep behind it.
mosaicJunior: Look at his hand — someone's showing him how to hold the pen.
mosaicJunior2: The bird-headed one is Thoth. Writing, counting, keeping the records — all his.
mosaicJunior3: The ibis we followed up the river? That's his bird. Every number we've filled into a wall belongs to him too.
mosaicExpert: That light isn't luck. They built the whole hall so it would land right there, on the right morning.
mosaicExpert2: The sun is Amun-Ra — the hidden one, and the light everyone can see. Both at once.
mosaicExpert3: Anyone who can measure the sky that precisely can measure anything. We've been solving their arithmetic all this way.
mosaicMaster: Green skin, and wheat growing straight out of him. That's on purpose.
mosaicMaster2: Osiris. He was killed, and put back together, and now he's what comes back every year when the river floods the fields.
mosaicMaster3: Down here that's the whole idea: dead isn't finished. Cheerful thought for a tomb, isn't it?
mosaicWizard: A heart on one side. One feather on the other. And it's balancing.
mosaicWizard2: The feather is Ma'at — truth, balance, the way things are supposed to be. Heavier heart than that feather and you don't go through the door.
mosaicWizard3: The jackal steadying the scale is Anubis. He's the one who walks you here.
mosaicFinale: Stand back a moment. Look at what we've been carrying up out of those pyramids.
mosaicFinale2: Every piece is part of him — the one who steadies the scale. He's been watching the whole way.
mosaicFinale3: That's his record of us. And I'd say it balances.
shopFirstVisit: Ah, here we are. My stall — I did say I was in this for the trade.
shopFirstVisit2: Everything on this counter I carried out of somewhere. That one came from two tombs back.
shopArrival: Ah, my stall! Let me lay out what I've picked up along the way.
shopArrival2: Rare finds cost the most, but I've also got everyday supplies — and I'll pay you for any trinkets you're carrying.

1.explorer: There is writing on it. Down at the base, where the sand keeps shifting off.

2.explorer: I cannot read a word of it.

6.fez: The base was painted, you know. All of it. Blue and gold, to about here.

9.fez: Fez. I'm along for the trade — those tombs are full of things worth selling.

1.fez: Now this I understand. Everything that ever went up the Nile came past here first.

2.fez: And merchants write it all down. Who bought what, who owed whom, who was late.

5.fez: Three thousand years, and the receipts outlived the goods. Typical.

1.fez: People came here to ask for protection, and protection meant a door that stays shut.

3.fez: Anyone who didn't ask nicely. Us, mainly.

4.fez: Every sealed thing in this country was sealed by someone who meant it.

5.fez: And the cats! They kept cats here, you know. Adored them. Couldn't help themselves.

1.fez: This is where they were taught. Sign by sign, on broken pottery — papyrus was far too dear to waste on children.

3.fez: They practised on what there was. Learn enough of these and a wall stops being decoration.

4.explorer: I want another look at that Sphinx.

1.fez: They came back every year with the flood, near enough to the day.

2.fez: So people started counting the days between. That is where the calendar comes from — birds.

4.fez: Birds and paperwork. It is always birds and paperwork.

1.fez: This is where they made it all. Not the tombs — the things that went in them.

2.fez: Look at the moulds. Same bracelet, forty times.

4.fez: For anyone who could pay. A noble wanted what a king had, at a price a noble could bear.

1.fez: Thoth, this one. God of secrets and magic, I am fairly sure.

3.fez: Ninety per cent. Anyway — the signs you have been collecting are his.

1.fez: Three hundred feet of it, and a fire at the top that never went out.

2.fez: Sailors could find the coast from a day away. Before that they found it by hitting it.

3.explorer: How do you find anything out here without one?

4.fez: You ask someone who has been. That is my entire profession.

1.fez: Sixty-odd tombs cut into one valley, and every single one of them opened before we got here.

4.fez: What do you make of it?

1.fez: Amun-Ra. The sun. Everybody's favourite, and you can see why — look at the size of the place.

3.fez: Same god, I think. They doubled up on the popular ones.

1.fez: The whole country is a line of green either side of one river, and then it opens out here into this.

3.explorer: Which of those are we here for?

1.fez: The first one. Before this, kings went under a flat slab like everyone else.

2.fez: Someone stood here and thought: what if we did that, but six times, upwards.

4.fez: It is still standing and he is not. Depends what you mean.

1.fez: Two million blocks. Somebody counted.

3.fez: Somebody always counts. That is the part people forget about all this — it was run by clerks.

4.fez: Beautiful, isn't it. Hate to think what the payroll looked like.

1.fez: Instructions. That is all it is — what to say, in what order, so the journey goes properly.

3.fez: A manual for being dead. They wrote everything down, this lot.

4.fez: Which, given what we are looking for, is the first good news all week.

1.fez: Ah. Somebody's camp.

3.fez: Recent-ish. Tinned food and a bad cough, by the look of it.

4.fez: They went in further than this and they did not take their kit with them.

5.explorer: Did they come back for it?

1.fez: Now THIS is what the others were imitating. Look at the colour — three thousand years and it is still wet-looking.
The sun goes under the world at night and comes up the other side. That is the whole belief.

2.fez: Twelve hours in the dark, with things in the way, and somebody has to carry it through.

3.explorer: That is what we have been doing.

4.fez: I had been trying not to say so.

5.explorer: The sand is still coming in.

6.fez: It has been coming in for three thousand years. It does not stop, it just goes round.

7.fez: Fills up, turns over, starts again. Same as the sun.

1.fez: The scale. Heart on one side, feather on the other — so a good heavy heart wins, presumably.

2.explorer: Which way does a heavy thing go?

1.fez: The capstone goes on last and it goes on gold, so the whole thing catches first light.

3.fez: Anyone looking. That was the point — it was never for the man inside.

1.ipi: Took your time. Third shelf, the jar with the chip out of it — that one's mine. The rest you may as well have.

3.explorer: The jar said the third shelf.

4.ipi: I kept these accounts for forty years. I am not leaving them in that state.

5.ipi: You want to get on? Then there's a noblewoman north of here. Painted vault, very pleased with herself. She never paid for the lapis.

7.ipi: Henut, daughter of Sennefer, of the western estates. Eleven deben of lapis, unpaid, third year.

8.ipi: Of course she has a name. I wrote it down.

9.ipi: It is the Horis that finish you. Hori the boatman, Hori the baker, and the other Hori.

11.ipi: In one street? Four. I had to put their fathers in as well.

12.explorer: Why does that matter, if she is not here to hear it?

13.ipi: Because a thing written down is a thing that happened. Rub out a man's name and he never did.

14.ipi: Tell her Ipi sent you. That should spoil her afternoon.

15.fez: He'd have had cats, a man like this. Everyone did. Charming animals.

16.ipi: I had four, and not one of them was charming. They were for the grain.

17.ipi: Do you know what a rat costs you, over a season? I do. To the sack.

20.ipi: Of course I wrote it down.

22.explorer: You like that he's owed money.

23.fez: I like that he wrote it down.

1.henut: Finally. You will have come about the lapis. I assume Ipi is still going on about the lapis.

3.henut: It was glass. Beautiful glass. He knew.

5.henut: Everything here is the best imitation money could buy, young man, and I chose every piece of it myself.

6.henut: Now. The wall. Third sign along — that is not my name. Some apprentice with a chisel and no supervision.

7.henut: You have been learning your signs. I can tell. Fix it.

8.henut: There. Now it will still be my name in a thousand years.

10.henut: Ipi spelled everything correctly. It was his one redeeming feature.

12.henut: It is the only thing that does.

13.fez: She had a whole wall of Thoth up there. God of secrets.

14.henut: Thoth counts. Thoth writes down what you did and it stays written.

15.henut: Secrets are what people call arithmetic when they cannot do it.

16.henut: If you are going on — and you clearly are — there is a priest at Karnak who owes the dead a service he never performed. He will be insufferable about it. Priests are.

1.priest: You are not the person I am expecting.

3.priest: Somebody with the seal. It was to be brought here, set down there, and spoken over. None of those three things has happened.

5.priest: I do not keep count. It would be unprofessional.

6.priest: A proper offering is a thing a king was buried holding. Not a copy. Not a likeness. The thing itself, with his mark on it.

7.priest: Bring that and you will be announced. Bring anything else and you will not.

9.priest: You will know. Everybody does, eventually.

10.fez: He is very taken with the sun, this one. All that Amun-Ra out front.

11.priest: Amun is the hidden one. Ra is the one anybody can see.

12.priest: They are the same god. That is not a coincidence, it is the entire idea.

1.fez: Nobody has been in here. Not us, not the earlier lot, nobody.

3.fez: Because there is still something in it.

1.pharaoh: You may approach. You have approached. Very well.

5.pharaoh: So does everyone. Mine has been taken twice and returned never.

6.pharaoh: The second time they left a copy. A COPY. In MY tomb. As though I would not look.

8.pharaoh: Of course it is still here, it is worthless. It is on the shelf where the real one should be, being wrong.

9.pharaoh: Take it if you like. Take it to that priest. See how far it gets you.

11.pharaoh: I am having the best week in nine hundred years.

12.fez: Osiris on the wall there. Lord of the dead — grim business.

13.pharaoh: He is GREEN, you ridiculous animal.

14.pharaoh: Green like a field in flood. He was killed and put back together and he comes back every single year.

15.pharaoh: Down here that is not grim, it is the entire point. Dead is not finished.

3.priest: That is the first time I have done that. I had begun to think I had forgotten how.

1.fez: Their rope. Still tied off.

3.fez: Further than this. And then they went back up it.

6.explorer: Cannot read the writing. Came back for the seal. Made a better one instead.

8.fez: …They forged it because they could not read what it was for.

1.fez: Stop a moment. Look at what we have been carrying up out of those pyramids.

3.fez: It has been a picture the whole time.
